full_judgment:
Borhanuddin J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 21-3-2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj, in Title Suit No. 10 of 2001 dismissing the suit.
2. The appellants being plaintiffs filed Title suit No 207 of 1997 in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Narayanganj which was subsequently renumbered as Title suit No. 10 of 2001. The plaintiffs instituted the suit with the following prayers:—
উপরোক্ত যাবতীয় অবস্থাধীনে বাদীগণের বিনীত প্রার্থনা,
(ক) নিম্ন তপসিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিতে বাদীগণের ষোল আনা স্বত্ব ঘোষণার ডিক্রি দিতে।
(খ) আরজীর এনেক্সার ১ মূলে নালিশী সম্পত্তি মধ্যে ৬৫ শতাংশ ভুমি সরকারের খাস সম্পত্তি মর্মে ঘোষণা ও দাবী বে-আইনী, এখতিয়ার বিহীন, তঞ্চকতাপূর্ণ, অকার্যকর এবং বাদীগণের প্রতি প্রযোজ্য নহে মর্মে ঘোষণার ডিক্রি দিতে।
(গ)-------
(ঘ)-------
3. Plaintiff's case, in a nutshell, is that Santosh Kumar Roy Chowdhury, Ashok Kumar Roy Chowdhury, Nihar Ranjan Roy Chowdhury, Joggeshar Roy Chowdhury, Amullay Roy Chowdhury, Binodini Roy Chowdhury, Profulla Roy Chowdhury, Souda-moni Roy Chowdhury, Anup Roy Chowdhury, Bhanu Roy Chowdhury, Haripada Roy Chowdhury, Kanu Roy Chowdhury, Dipali Roy Chowdhury, Nibedita Roy Chowdhury, Sanjib Roy Chowdhury got saham in the suit schedule land along with other properties in Partition Suit No. 12 of 1938 which was decreed on 13-12-1958 by the learned Sub-Judge, Second Court, Comilla and entered into possession through execution decree dated 21-3-1961 and since then they owned and possessed the land as successors of their predecessors without any hindrance.
4. During possession said Santosh Kumar Roy Chowdhury, Ashok Kumar Roy Chowdhury, Nihar Ranjan Roy Chowdhury, Mrilani Roy Chowdhury, Amullay Roy Chowdhury and Binodini Roy Chowdhury transferred 29'4, decimals and from CS Plot Nos. 400 and 6 to the plaintiff No. 1 vide registered deed No. 107 dated 4-1-1964 and delivered possession thereof. Thereafter, Rai Mohan Chowdhury, constituted attorney of Profulla Roy Chowdhury, transferred 28 decimals of land from the same CS Plots to the plaintiff No. 1 through registered deed No. 5998 dated 11-7-1970 and delivered possession thereof. Surendra Roy Chowdhury, one of the saham holder in Partition suit No. 12 of 1938, died leaving 3 sons namely, Sukendu Roy Chowdhury, Haripada Roy Chowdhury, Ajit Kumar Roy Chowdhury and wife Soundamoni Roy Chowdhury as his heirs. Elder sun Sukendu Roy Chowdhury inherited 300/4 decimals of land in CS Plot No.400 and SA Plot No. 573 of the said partition suit along with other lands. Said Sukendu Roy Chowdhury died leaving 3 sons Anup Roy Chowdhury, Bhanu Roy Chowdhury, Kanu Roy Chowdhury and wife Dipali Roy Chowdhury as his heirs who in their turn transferred 7% decimals land as that share holders of 30% decimals land in CS Plot No. 400 and SA Plot No. 573 to the defendants No. 2 and 8 vide two registered deeds bearing Nos. 5553 and 5354 both dated 8-9-1976 and delivered possession thereof. Ajit Roy Chowdhury died leaving minor son Sanjib Roy Chowdhury and wife Nebadita Roy Chowdhury as his heirs who in their nun transferred 711/36 decimals land as 3/4th share holder 3034decimals land in CS Plot No. 400 and SA Plot No. 573 to the plaintiff No. 3 vide registered deed No. 5355 dated 8-9-1976 red delivered possession thereof. Said registered deed was executed by Amullay Roy Chowdhury, constituted attorney of the mother of minor Sanjib Roy Chowdhury.
5. Thereafter, Soundamoni Roy Chowdhury transferred 7h1/16 decimals of land as 1/4th Shareholder of 30% decimals of land in CS Plot No. 400 and SA Plot 573 and delivered possession thereof. Thus the plaintiffs became owners of the suit land along with other lands in CS Plot No. 400 and SA Plot No. 573 by way of purchase. The plaintiffs after purchase developed the land by filling earth and erecting a large one storied building thereon and since then they have been residing there with the members of their family. The plaintiffs also established one knitting factory, one filling station and planting valuable trees thereon. The plaintiffs mutated khatians in their names and regularly paying rents and municipal taxes. It has been further stated that on 7-7-1997 defendant No. 2 issued a Memo bearing No. এস.এ/ক-২৭-৫২৪ (2oo) under section 92 (I)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act extinguishing proprietary right in 65 decimals of land of SA Plot No. 573 and RS Plot No. 79 and 80 and asked to submit objection, if any, within 30 days in the office of the defendant No.-3. Being informed about the said Memo dated 7-7-1997 the plaintiffs submitted their registered title deeds, rent receipts and other relevant documents in the office of the defendant No. 3 with an objection that the suit land is not a vested property and there is no reason to extinguish their proprietary right in the land. After scrutinizing the documents submitted by the plaintiffs, the defendant No. 3 informed them that the suit land was never included in the censor list and the same is not leased out to any one, but in the RS Khatian the lands are recorded as vested property.
6. It has also been stated that recently the plaintiffs came to know from the office of the defendant No. 3 that the defendant No. 2 had included the suit land in Khas Khatian No.1. They were also informed from the said office that the defendants are trying to lease out the suit land to the defendant No. 4. Thereafter, on 26-11-1997 the plaintiff No. 2 procured the certified copy of the RS Khatian and found in the said Khatian Krantee share recorded in the name of the plaintiff No. 1 and other shares recorded in the names of their vendors but at the end of column 2 of the said RS Khatian, present address of the recordees is written as "'11\D It 1-tm-A1 mod" The said RS Khatian was prepared and published wrongly. It is stated that at the time of preparation of the said RS Khatian, the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 were minors and students and plaintiff No. 1 being less educated, and also for his blindness could not take steps, which resulted such wrong recording. It has also been stated that there is no reason to extinguish proprietary right of the plaintiffs in the suit land under section 92(1)(e) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, or to be treated the same as vested property. Wrong recording of present address in RS Khatian and Memo dated 7-7-1997 under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, issued by the defendant No. 2, claiming the suit land as khas, has clouded title of the plaintiffs for which the plaintiffs are constrained to institute the present suit.
7. The defendants No. 1 to 3 filed a joint written statement denying the materials allegations made in the plaint and contenting interlaid that the suit is not maintainable in its present form and barred by the principles of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel. Their further contentions are that the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land. The sale deeds are forged, created and not acted upon. It has been further contended that after SA recorded tenants abandoned the suit land, the same is treated as khas land under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Transfer of Khas land in any manner is illegal and void. As the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest in the suit land, and suit is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed with cost.
8. The defendant No. 4 neither filed any written statement in the suit nor contested the same.
9. The plaintiffs adduced 3 witnesses and defendant adduced 1 witness to prove their respective cases. After hearing the parties, the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj, dismissed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 21-3-2004 (decree signed on 24-3-2004) holding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their right, title and interest in the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint.
10. Heaving aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree, the plaintiffs being appellants preferred the instant appeal.
11. Mr Md Abdul Alim Miah, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submitted that the plaintiffs purchased the suit land from the owners who acquired their right, title and interest therein through Judgment and decree dated 13-12-1958 in Partition Suit No. 12 of 1938 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla and entered into possession through Execution Case No. 55 of 1960. Said title holders of the suit land during possession executed and registered sale deeds in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs mutated Khatians in their names and regularly paying rents in the Tahsil Office and municipal taxes in the municipality which were accepted by the relevant offices without any objection. The learned Advocate also submitted that the trial Court erred in law in disbelieving the exhibits filed by the plaintiffs without any .cogent reason though 'no objection was raised by the defendants at the time of admission of those exhibits. In this regard, the learned Advocate referred to the 'case of Joynal Abedin vs Hafizur Rahman, reported in 13 BLD (AD) 150 = 44 DLR (AD) 162 and also the case of Abdullah vs Abdul Karim, reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205. The learned Advocate also submitted that it is admitted by the defendants that the suit property was never included in the census list and the government has never taken possession of the land and, as such, wrong recording of present address in the RS Khatian can not extinguish the proprietary right of the plaintiffs acquired by registered title deeds. In this regard he referred to the case of Bangladesh vs Md Shahjahan, reported in 20 BLD (AD) 166. He next submitted that the trial Court erred in law in discarding the registered sale deeds of Asgar Ali Miah executed and registered more than 30 days ago and thus violates the provisions of section 90 of the Evidence Act. In this regard, he referred to the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) vs Md Reazuddin Pk, reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76 and also the case of Kamaruddin @ Fakira vs Anisur Rahman, report-ed in 1 BLC 102. He also submitted that since the defendant No. 2 issued Memo under section 92(1)(c) of the SAT Act, extinguishing the proprietary right in the suit land declaring the same as Khas land, onus lies on the defendants to prove that the original raiyats abandoned the suit land without making any arrangement for payment of rent as it falls due. In this regard, he referred to the case of Gita Rani vs Bangladesh, reported in 36 DLR (AD) 225. The learned Advocate also submitted that in discarding the sale deeds executed and. registered under Registration Act, 1908 the trial Court violates the provisions of section 68 of the Evidence Act. In this regard, the learned Advocate referred to the case of Md Rafiq vs Md Zahur Nasir, reported in 8 DLR (WP) Lahore 56. He further submitted that after purchasing the suit land, the plaintiffs established filling station by taking permission from the defendant No. 2 which is evident from 'Exhibit-6. With such submissions, the learned Advocate prays to allow the appeal by setting aside the judgment and decree passed the by the trial Court.
12. Mr Shashanka Shekhor Sarker, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, on the other hand, appearing for the respondents No. 1, 2 and 3 supported the judgment passed. by the learned Joint District Judge. He submitted that the instant suit for declaration of title is not maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, without seeking consequential relief relating to the wrong recording of RS Khatian. He next submitted that the Khatians in the name of the plaintiffs No. 2 and 3, executed and registered in the year 1976 are forged, inoperative and not acted upon. In elaborating his submission, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submitted that in the year 1976 when those sale deeds were executed and registered, the plaintiff's No. 2 and 3 were minors and it is settled principle of law that the minors can not enter into any contract. To-day at the time of delivery of the judgment, the learned Deputy Attorney-General raised the point of limitation, submitting that the plaintiffs did not filed the instant suit within 90 days from the date of order of the Revenue Officer under sub-section (3) of section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as prescribed in sub-section (4) ibid.
13. Mr Syed Mokaddas Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 4 adopted the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney-General. It is earlier mentioned that the respondent No. 4, who was imp leaded as defendant No. 4 in the suit, neither filed any written statement nor contested the suit.
14. We have carefully gone through the judgment passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Narayanganj.
In disposing the suit, the trial Court framed the following issues:
১। মামলাটি বর্তমান আকার ও প্রকারে চলিতে পারে কি না?
২। নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বাদীদের স্বার্থ ও দখল আছে কিনা?
৩। বাদীগণ প্রার্থীত মতে নালিশী তপশিলের সম্পত্তিতে ষোল আনা স্বত্ব ঘোষণার ডিক্রী পাতে পারে কিনা?
৪। বাদীগণ অন্য কোন প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে কিনা?
15. Upon a close reading of the impugned judgment it appears that the learned Judge emphasized mainly on the genuineness of the sale deeds executed and registered in favour of the plaintiffs. In discarding the registered sale deeds of the plaintiff No. 1 Asgar Ali Miah, the trial Court observed that:
“বাদীর ১নং সাক্ষী ২নং বাদী মাসুদুজ্জামান এর জেরায় এই দলিল দুই খানা দীর্ঘ ৩০ (ত্রিশ) বছরের পুরাতন হিসাবে সাক্ষ্য আইনের ৯০ ধারা মত প্রদর্শনী চিহ্নিত করান হয়। তবে দলিলগুলির হেফাজতের কারণে প্রদর্শনী করা হইলেও তাহা যে বিশুদ্ধ বলিয়া ধরিয়াই চুড়ান্ত সিদ্ধান্ত নিতে হইবে এই ধারায় এমন কথা নাই এবং তাহা গ্রহণে যথেষ্ট সাবধানতা অবলম্বন করাই সংগত বিধায় হেফাজতের দাবীতে প্রদর্শনীতে আনিয়া দলিল লিখক বা দলিলের সাক্ষী দিয়া সাক্ষ্য প্রদানে প্রমাণে না নিবার অবস্থায় ২নং বাদীর সাক্ষ্যের আলোকে দলিল সন্দেহ মুক্ত ভাবে বলা যায় না।”
16. Those two registered sale deeds were exhibited by PW 1. who is the son of Asgar Ali Miah and also the defendant No. 2 in the suit. It appears from the above observation that the trial Court did not discard those two registered sale deeds for not having produced from the proper custody but on the ground of non-examination of scribe or the attesting witnesses. In the case of Additional Deputy C011111-litiSi011Ci" (Revenue) vs Md Reazuddin Pk , reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76, our appellate Division held :
"Once such a document more than 30 years old is produced from proper custody, section 90 of the Evidence Act entitles the Court to presume that it is a genuine document"
<u><u>17. Thus the learned Joint District Judge violates the provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act in not taking into consideration of the documents since those are 30 years old and produced from custody.</u></u>
18. Section 68 of the Evidence Act, deals with proof of execution of document required by law. Section 68 of the Evidence Act, runs as follows:—
"68. Proof of execution of document required by Law to be attested : If a document is required by law to be attested, it shall not be used as evidence until one attesting witness at least has been called for purpose of proving its execution, if there be an attesting witness alive, and subject to the process of the Court and capable of giving evidence: [Provided that it shall not be necessary to call an attesting witness in proof of the execution of any document, not being a will, which has been registered in accordance with the provisions of the Registration Act, 1908, unless its, execution by the person by whom it purports to have been executed is specifically denied.]"
<u><u>19. Admittedly in the present case, the executants did not deny the execution of those registered sale deeds. In fact, none denied the execution of those deeds. No one challenged the deeds in a competent Court of law. Thus, it is clear that the observation of the learned Joint District Judge is contrary to the proviso of section 68 of the Evidence Act.</u></u>
20. The trial Court also discarded the registered deed No. 4344 dated 7-7-1976 with the following finding:
“নিবেদিতা রায় চৌধুরী পতি মৃত অজিত কুমার রায় চৌধুরী স্বয়ং ও নাবালক পুত্র সজীব রায় চৌধুরী পিতা অজিত কুমার রায় চৌধুরী পক্ষে স্বাভাবিক অভিভাবিকা মাতা হইতে পাইবার দাবী করা হয়। কিন্তু নাবালক পুত্রের হস্তান্তরের ক্ষেত্রে মাতা উপযুক্ত আদালত হইতে অভিভারিকা নিয়োগ সহ বিক্রির অনুমতির কোন সনদ নাই।”
21. Section 6 of The Hindu Minority and Guardianship Aa, 1956 provides that the natural guardians of a Hindu minor, in respect of the minor's person as well as in respect of the minor's property (Excluding his or her undivided interest in joint family property), are —(a) in the case of a boy or an unmarried girl—the father, and after him, the mother; provided that the custody of a minor who has not completed the age of five years shall ordinarily be with the mother.
22. It is admitted that in the instant Case father Ajit Kumar Roy Chowdhury died leaving his minor son Santosh Kumar Roy Chowdhury and wife Nibedita Roy Chowdhury. In Mulla's 'Principle of Hindu Law' powers of natural guardian narrated as follows:
"Powers of Natural Guardian—The powers of a natural guardian under Hindu Law as hitherto applied have been dealt with in sections 528-531 ante. The rights of a natural guardian under that law as interpreted by the Courts were comparatively wide. The natural guardian, as must have been seen from section 528, could mortgage, charge, sell or otherwise dispose of the immoveable Property, even without the sanction of the Court, provided the alienation or any other dealing with such property by the guardian was for the benefit of the minor's estate."
23. In the said registered deed No 5355 dated 8-9-1976, it has been categorically stated that:
“এইক্ষণ আমার ও আমার নাবালক পুত্রের খোরাক পোষাক ও বিদ্যাশিক্ষার ব্যয় নির্বাহার্থে নগদ টাকার বিশেষ দরকার হওয়ায় নিম্ন তফছিল বর্ণিত নাল জমির ১/০ চারি আনা অংশ বিক্রয় করার মত প্রকাশ করিলে আপনি দলিল গ্রহিতা উতা ক্রয় করিতে ইচ্ছুক হইয়াছেন।”
<u><u>24. The foretasted statements simply proves that mother Nibedita Roy Chowdhury transferred the property as a natural guardian of the benefit of her minor son. As such, we are of the view that the findings of the trial Court in this regard are contrary to the law and also 'perverse for misreading of evidence on record.</u></u>
25. Admittedly, the plaintiffs mutated khatians in their names and regularly paying rents and taxes. The trial Court in discarding
“উল্লেখ্য আর, এস খতিয়ান সম্পত্তি খাস অবস্থায় বাদীপক্ষ, কিভাবে খাজনার দাখিলা (প্রদর্শনী ৩ ও ১১ সিরিজ) অর্জন করিয়াছেন তাহা বোধগম্য না।”
26. The relevant RS Khatian was prepared in the year 1969 to 1970 and finally published in the year 1980 but the impugned Memo under section 92(1)(c) issued on 7-7-1997 by the respondent No. 2 extinguishing proprietary right in the suit land. We failed to understand how the trial Court observe, that the land was recorded khas in the said RS Khatian.
27. It is true that PW 1 stated in his cross-examination that he was born in the year 1964 and the sale deeds were executed and registered in the year 1976. For the aforesaid reason the trial Court disbelieved those sale deeds with the following findings
“এই স্বাক্ষীর জেরায় তাহার জন্ম হয় ১৯৬৪ সালে অর্থাৎ (১৯৭৬-১৯৬৪)=১২ বৎসর বয়সে তাহার এবং তাহার ছোট ভাই আরও ছোট ছিল অবস্থায় এই বয়সে তাহাদের সম্পত্তি খরিদের উৎস ও অস্পষ্ট, তাই এই দলিলগুলির সম্পত্তি সঠিক ভাবে হস্তান্তর বিশ্বাসযোগ্য নয়।”
<u><u>28. Admittedly, those sale deeds were registered under section 60 of the Registration Act. Since those deeds being registered documents under section 60 of the Registration Act, a strong Presumption is attached to those deed as the privy council stated in 33 IA 60 "what remains to be shown is that the person admitting execution before the registrar was this Purushotam Das and no imposter. The question is one of fact expect insofar as there was as matter of law a presumption that the registration proceedings were regular and honestly carried out."</u></u>
29. Whether contract with minor is enforceable by and against him, was discussed elaborately in the case of Ashraf Ali vs Etim Ali, reported in 11 DLR 185, wherein this Division held:
"In an executed contract where the minor's part has been performed and nothing is left to be executed by the minor, i.e. no obligation is left to be discharged by the minor and to be enforced against him, such a contract is enforceable by the minor as it is a contract for the benefit of the minor, such as completed by sale or mortgage in favour of the minor and is enforceable by law."
It is further held:—
"Sections 10 and 11 of the contract Act, enacted for the benefit and protections of the minor cannot be made to separa to against the minor.
"Fact remains that the case in land is not a case for cancellation of the aforementioned sale deeds on the ground that those are forged, fraudulent, inoperative and not acted upon. In fact, no one challenged those sale deeds in a competent Court of law. The trial Court failed to consider that those deeds are registered instruments and registered in accordance with law. .After registration of those deeds, the plaintiffs developed the land by filling earth and possessing the same by erecting building, established Knittirig factoiy, filling station with the permission of the defendants and planted various trees thereon. The plaintiffs also mutated khatians in their names and paying rents and taxes thereof.
30. The trial Court at the very outset held that the suit is not maintainable for not identifying the suit land. The defendants neither in the written statement nor in the deposition challenged the identity of the suit land. The defendants also used the word suit land while describing their case. The defendants did not say anywhere the land claimed by them was not the land described by in the schedule of the plaint. Moreover, in the local inspection report, the land is described by a sketch map demarcating the boundary which is evident from the lower Court's record. In view of the above position, we do not understand why the learned Joint District Judge came to a finding that the suit land is not identifiable.
31. On perusal of the judgment, it appears that the trial Court is completely silent relating to prayer "Kha" of the plaint. By prayer (Kha), the plaintiffs prayed for a declaration that the Memo dated 7-7-1977 issued by the defendant No. 2 under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. is illegal, inoperative and not binding upon them.
32. To begin with section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, may be noticed the terms which are as follows:
"92(1) The interest of a raiyat in a holding shall be extinguished—(a) when he dies interstate leaving no heir entitled to inherit under the law of inheritance to which he is subject;
(b) when he surrenders his holding at the end of any agricultural year by giving notice in the prescribed form and in the prescribed manner and within the prescribed period of the Revenue-officer,
(c) when he voluntarily abandons his residence without making any arrangement for payment of the rent as it falls due and ceases to cultivate his holding either by himself or by members of his family or by, or with the aid of, servants or laborers with the aid of partners or bargaders for a period of the three successive years, or
(d) when such interest has devolved by inheritance, under the law of inheritance to which such raiyat is subject, on a person who is not a bona fide cultivator and such person has not cultivated the land comprised in the holding either by himself or by members of his family or by, or with the aid of, servants or labourers or with the aid of partners or bargaders during the period of five years from the date on which such in interest has so devolved on him and there is no sufficient why he has not so cultivated the land.
(2) When the interest of a raiyat in a holding is extinguished under sub-section (1), the Revenue-officer may enter on the holding; and the holding shall, with effect from the date of which the Revenue-officer so enters on it, vest absolutely in the [Government] free from all encumbrances except the encumbrances on the holding which is extinguished under clause (a) of the said sub-section, but the persons whose interest in the holdings are extinguished under clauses (b), (c) and (d) of the sub-section shall continue to be personally liable for the money secured by the encumbrances on such holdings.
(3) Before entering on a holding under sub-section (2), the Revenue-officer shall cause as notice to so enter on be published in the prescribed manner declaring his intention to so enter on the holding and specifying the reasons thereof and also inviting objections from all persons interested in the holding and shall consider any objections that may be submitted to him within the period specified in that behalf in the notice and shall record a decision.
(4) Any person aggrieved by an order passed by the Revenue-officer Under sub-section (3). on any objection shown against the extinguishment of the interest of any raiyat in this holding under clause (d) or sub-section (1) may, instead of filing any appeal under section 147, institute a suit in the Civil Court against such order. Not-withstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, such suit shall be filed within ninety days from the date of the order of the Revenue-officer under sub-section (3).
(5) All arrears of rent in respect of a holding remaining due from a raiyat whose interest in such holding has been extinguished under sub-section (1) shall be deemed to irrecoverable.
<u><u>33. The impugned Memo issued by the defendant No. 2 is under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, which provides the interest of a raiyat in a holding shall be extinguished when he voluntarily abandons his residence without making any arrangement of the rent as it falls due and ceases to cultivate his holding either by himself or by members of his family or bargaders for a period of three successive years. But in the present case, it is admitted that the plaintiffs are regularly paying rents and taxes in the Tahashil Office and municipality which were accepted by the relevant officers without any objection.</u></u>
<u><u>34. The defendant's case is that, since the original raiyat left the suit land, the suit property is escheated to the Government under section 92(1)(c) of the SAT Act. But in imposing section 92(1)(c) of SAT Act the onus is on the defendants to prove that the original raiyat abandoned the suit land without making any arrangement of the rent as it falls due. In the case of Gita Rani vs Bangladesh reported in 36 DLR (AD) 226, our Apex Court held:</u></u>
<u><u>"When the claim is founded on escheat the onus lies on it that the owner estate died without heir. In Grida Lal vs Bengal Government (1868) 12 MIA 448 the privy council laid down that the onus is on the Government to show that the last proprietor of the land died without heir. This proposition still holds the field and therefore it is too late in the day to take a contrary view."</u></u>
35. In the case of Sree jukta Haladhar Karmakar vs Bangladesh, reported in 16 BLD 519, this division held :
"A statement in the plaint or in the written statement is no evidence in the eye of law unless it is proved by examining a witness on oath. In the instant suit the defendants claimed that the original owners had left this country before 1965 and the suit property became enemy property by operation of law. The onus was upon the defendant to prove that fact either by examining any witness or by producing any reliable documentary evidence establishing that the real owners had left this country before 1965. In the absence of such evidence the property in question cannot be treated as enemy property or vested property. "
36. In the case on hand the 'Exhibits-'3' and H' i.e. the 'rent receipts' amply proves that the plaintiffs are regularly paying rents and taxes for the suit property and the said rents and taxes were accepted by the relevant authority without raising any objection. When the defendant No. 2 issued Memo under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act extinguishing the proprietary right, the onus is on the defendants to prove that the raiyats voluntarily abandoned the land without making any arrangement for payment of rent as it falls due. But the defendants 'miserably failed to establish their case that the original raiyats voluntarily abandoned the land in question by producing any reliable documentary evidence or that the sale deeds executed and registered in favour of the plaintiffs are forged and not acted upon or that the rent receipts exhibited by the plaintiffs are false and forged.
<u><u>37. The learned Deputy Attorney-General raised the question of maintainability of the suit for not seeking consequential relief relating to the RS Khatian wherein present address of the plaintiffs is wrongly recorded. It is admitted that no notice was served upon the plaintiffs before issuance of the Memo under section 92(1)(c) dated 7-7-1997 though the plaintiffs admittedly possessing the land on payment of rents and taxes regularly. It is categorically stated in the plaint that being informed about the said Memo, the plaintiff submitted their registered title deeds, rent receipts, and other relevant documents in the office of defendant No. 3 with an objection that the suit land is not a vested property and there is no reason to extinguish their proprietary right therein. After scrutinizing plaintiffs documents the defendant No. 3 informed them that the suit land was never included in the census list and same is not leased out to anyone but in the RS Khatian the lands are recorded as vested property. Then the plaintiffs applied for the certified copy of the RS Khatian and after procuring the certified copy on 26-11-1997, the plaintiffs for the first time came to know that the RS Khatian is wrongly prepaid. Earlier they did not enquired about the same because Tahsil Office or any other department never raised any objection in receiving the rent or taxes or accorded permission for establishing filling station on the land.</u></u>
38. In the case of Karimunnessa being dead her heirs Chand Ali Pramanik vs Sorab Ali, reported in 8 BLC 255, this Division held :
"Mere knowledge about the wrong recording of SA Khatian does not give rise to the cause of action to bring any suit, if the plaintiff does not bring such cause of action in the plaint. Limitation shall start running from the date of given cause of action."
It is further held:
"In a simple suit for declaration of title when some of the DWs admitted possession of the plaintiffs in some portion of the suit land it can not be said that the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act."
On perusal of the record, it is evident that the defendants in their several letters, internal communication and reports admitted the pos-session of the plaintiffs in the suit land. Even the DW 1 admitted in his cross-examination that “নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে দালান, নিটিং মিল, পেট্রাল পাম্প, গাছ পালা আছে। He further stated in his cross “খাজনার দাখিলা তহশিল অফিস হইতে ইস্যু করা হয়। এই ধরনের ফার্মেই আমরা খাজনা নেই।”
<u><u>39. After obtaining the certified copy of the RS Khatian on 26-11-1997, plaintiffs filed the present suit on 30-11-1997. In the plaint cause of action clearly stated in paragraph No. 13.“১৩। নালিশের কারণে বিগত ২৭-৭-৯৭ ইং এবং ২৬-১১-৯৭ এই তারিখে ও তদন্তে অত্রাদালতের এলাকাধীন থানা ফতুল্লার অন্তর্গত খানপুর ‘ম’ খন্ড মৌজায় উদ্ভব হইয়াছে।” In view of the said averments relating to cause of action and several letters, internal communications and reports of the defendants and also in view of the deposition of DW 1 admitting possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land, it can not be said that the suit is barred by section 42 of the specific Relief Act.</u></u>
40. In the circumstances, relying on the decision referred above, we hold that the suit instituted by the plaintiff-appellants for declaration of title of the suit schedule land without seeking consequential relief is main-tainable.
41. Another point raised by the learned Deputy Attorney-General that the suit is barred by limitation under Sub-section (4) of section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. for not filing it within 90 days from the date of the order of the Revenue Officer under sub-section (3) of section 92 ibid.
42. On perusal of the record, it is apparent that no notice was served upon the plaintiffs under sub-section (3) of section 92 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, though admittedly they are in possession of the suit land and regularly paying rents and taxes for the suit land. Rather, it appears from the record that notice under sub-section (3) of section 92 was issued in the name of Profulla Kumar Roy Chowdhury and others, who admittedly transferred the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs by the sale deeds executed and registered by them.
43. In the case of Bangladesh vs Sailesh Chandra Bhattacharya 'Vol.' IV' Bangladesh Supreme Court Digest, page 204, our Apex Court held:—
"Where no notice was issued by the Revenue-Officer under sub-section (3) of section 92 inviting any objection against the taking over the holding as "abandoned" holding, the period of limitation prescribed in that section will not be applicable and a case therefore attracts the general provisions of limitation under Article 120. of the Limitation Act."\48
44. Again, in the case of Hindu Deity Lakshmi Gobinda Jeu vs Deputy Custodian Enemy Property, reported in 51 DLR 300, their lordships held :—
"The provision of reinstitution of a suit in the Civil Court within 90 days of the order of the Government treating a property as an abandoned property does not provide any penal consequence for the failure of the aggrieved party to institute the suit within 90 days and, as such, it cannot be said that the aggrieved party is debarred from challenging the order of the government subsequently by instituting a suit."
<u><u>45. Since no notice was served upon the plaintiffs under section 92(3) of the SAT Act, and in view of the decisions referred herein-above, we hold that the suit is not barred by limitation.</u></u>
46. Under the facts and circumstance of the case, we are of the view that since the sale deeds executed in favour of the plaintiffs being registered documents under section 60 of the Registration Act, and the plaintiffs admittedly are in possession of the suit land pursuant to those sale deeds and since those registered sale deeds are not declared as forged, inoperative and not acted upon by a competent Court of law, the plaintiffs are entitled to get a declaration of title for the suit schedule land. As we have already mentioned that the plaintiffs are paying rents and taxes regularly after purchasing the suit schedule and land possessing the same by erecting building, establishing knitting factory, filling station and planting valuable trees thereon, which is also admitted by the defendants, and since the defendants failed to establish their case by producing any reliable documentary evidence that the original raiyats voluntarily abandoned the suit land or the exhibited sale deeds and rent receipts are forged or the plaintiffs are not in possession of the land, we are of the opinion that the impugned Memo dated 7-7-1997 under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act issued by the defendant No. 2 is not in conformity with the spirit of the said section of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.
47. It appears from the judgment of the trial Court that the findings of the learned Judge are perverse for non consideration and misreading of material evidence on record and also contrary to the provisions of law and, as such, liable to be set-aside.
48. For the reasons stated above, we hold that the appellants have acquired right, title and possession in the suit land and the impugned Memo dated 7-7-1997 under section 92(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, extinguishing the proprietary right in the suit land issued by the defendant No. 2 is hereby declared absolutely illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs.
49. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the suit is decreed.
50. The judgment and decree dated 21-3-2004 (decree signed on 24-3-2004) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit No. 10 of 2001 is hereby set-aside.
51. A supplementary cause list is prepared to dispose of the connected Civil Rule. As the appeal is allowed, the connected Civil Rule No. 171(F) of 2004 is disposed of accordingly.
However, there will be no order as to costs.
